logline: As the haze takes the harbor and then him, the poet refuses to leave, curses the ending, blesses the one he loved ('I trust that you'll be fine'), and chooses the door into a slow dance as the suite loops.
reading:
It opens as a plea, 'Don't make me leave', to go back where 'promises, hearts, spectrums of light-filled constellations are broken'. He escaped here for a reason: a 'sharpened key of answers', a 'more grounded bravado'. He curses whatever ended the moment ('damn you') and asks that it still 'feel love and lost'. Then a refusal: 'absent artificial escapes and machine learning strengths'. He will keep his highs and lows as resource materials, the impulse from battle scars, and the wisdom 'that brushes gray tones into our melanin'.

The turn is 14_L16, 'I trust that you'll be fine': anger becomes blessing. 'I escaped here for a reason' then repeats as a choice, not a flight. The images run from weather (haze, constellations) to the body (scars, gray in melanin) to a dance: 'two entwined muses' for 'a hot minute', and 'a genesis of a New Testament as it ends'. An ending that is also a beginning: the door closes and 01 starts again.
motifs: haze that turns what he built into weather
taken from the ground up, reluctantly
floating in black with no walls
the reel: the suite's objects flashing past
gray brushed into melanin: earned wisdom
the doubled self: two entwined muses
an old door with light under it
a slow-motion party he enters by choice

light_and_texture: First grey: layered vellum and tissue sheets rise over a photographic plate until only an ink eave-line is left. Then black: matte black card with one faint horizon strip, the puppet lit only by its own kraft edges and by the frames that flash past. Last, gold: one warm source through a door, spilling a cut yellow-gel wedge across the puppet, and archive silver inside the doorway.

fx.how: stacked tissue and vellum sheets slide up over the plate while it crossfades gen_69ee5bb28b → gen_91d2196345 → gen_bb8e6e2acf; the temple eave remains as an ink line on clear acetate, then lifts away
a torn-vellum mask edge rises up the puppet; below it the card desaturates to haze grey with an Orange Haze amber rim; the red piping is the last colour to go; hold 1.5 s at the chest
1.00–1.02 scale breathing on a 4 s cycle with grain; Dust Storm 1936 cropped to a thin horizon band that never closes
the reel_frame strip slides; holds shrink 12 → 8 → 5 → 3 → 2 frames, with black frame-lines between; projector flicker on the puppet
punched paper stars and confetti burst from the joined hands, falling in slow code
a yellow-gel wedge card, additive, widening with the door angle; the puppet swaps to a gold-rimmed version where the wedge hits
archive party at 40% with frame blending; cut-outs on 2s at half speed; gold bloom on highlights
the door closes; the light line under it shrinks to a point and goes; hold black, then 01 begins

passage.keep: L16 'I trust that you'll be fine' answered by Don't Be Afraid 1953, 'Someone you're fond of and trust'. The hand opening palm-up and staying open is a clean held gesture, and the doorway in the black is the ideal surface: vertical, bright, the only thing in the frame.
passage.better: Make the door big and near, two-thirds of frame height, built from the Electric House 1922 panel design so it reads as a card. Open it a hand's width as he speaks, then wider on 'fond of', so the archive's brightness grows with the gesture. Let the gold-gel wedge fall across the open palm. Carry emotion with a head swap (reluctant → softened) rather than rotation, and keep him standing, not floating, so the palm stays still.
alt_lines: 14_L01 'Don't make me leave': one hand reaches back toward the city and stops short; Travel/Cities 1947 (building dissolving in haze) opens in the last lit tower window of gen_91d2196345
14_L08 'Whatever has terminated this moment, damn you': grip into a fist, head lowers; Dust Storm 1936's white-out fills the horizon band and brightens on 'damn you'

14_L14–15 'wisdom that brushes gray tones into our melanin': fingertips to his beard, held, with the head swapped for the gray-touched card; Care of the Hair and Nails 1951 (arch_019e25f6-802c) plays in a single reel frame beside him
14_L18 'Our dance together is a victory': hands gripped with the grey double, still for a beat before the turn; Under Western Stars dancers play in the ring of floor beneath them like a record

ideas: Weather by plates: POET's back-view cut-out stands on a quay card while gen_69ee5bb28b crossfades to gen_91d2196345 and gen_bb8e6e2acf; the white temple's eave stays an ink line on acetate for 1 s, then lifts with the tissue

The machines unplug: on 14_L10 'absent artificial escapes and machine learning strengths' the reel drops every generated frame and runs only archive film (Scrooge 1935 window, Heavenly Bodies, The Reasons Why candles, Muscatatuck daisy), so the film itself does what the line says
The reel as a How You See It 1936 strip sliding past the floating puppet; gen_a0ef973cb6 (tambourine) and gen_a63bb494b1 (window) are the only generated callbacks before the cut-off
Gray in the beard: one head swap in the whole poem, to a card with gray brushed into the beard, held on 'melanin'; the double is painted in the same gray

The door arrives: first as a bright vertical slit in black (Harvest of the Years, arch_7ee2fb8e-98c9), which becomes the panelled door card; De Joodsche invalide 1939's hand-on-knob shot cut in as the knob turns

Into the archive: through the doorway, His Royal Highness 1932's crowded ballroom and Under Western Stars' pennants; paper couples dance in front, and he walks between them until his cut-out passes behind the film plane and is gone
Loop: the door closes, the gold line goes out, and the same door card hangs in black as the first frame of 01
